capital.name: Jakarta
capital.description: A dense metropolis on the northwest coast of Java, Jakarta is Indonesia's political and economic heart — a city of layered histories, waterfronts, and relentless energy.

landmarks.name: Borobudur
landmarks.description: The world's largest Buddhist temple, a ninth-century stone mandala of over two million blocks rising from the Kedu Plain.

landmarks.name: Bali
landmarks.description: Terraced rice fields, temple coastlines and volcanic ridges — the island of a thousand temples.

landmarks.name: Raja Ampat
landmarks.description: Four great islands adrift in a sea of coral — the most biodiverse marine habitat on Earth.

landmarks.name: Komodo National Park
landmarks.description: Pale volcanic islands ruled by the Komodo dragon, the largest living lizard on the planet.

landmarks.name: Mount Bromo
landmarks.description: An active volcano standing inside a vast caldera of sand, crowned by the Sea of Sand.

foods.name: Rendang
foods.description: Beef slow-cooked for hours in coconut milk and a complex paste of chilies, lemongrass and spices until deeply caramelized.

foods.name: Nasi Goreng
foods.description: Indonesia's fragrant wok-fried rice, seasoned with sweet soy, shallots and chili, crowned with a fried egg.

foods.name: Satay
foods.description: Skewers of marinated meat grilled over charcoal, glazed with sweet soy and served with peanut sauce.

foods.name: Gado-Gado
foods.description: A vibrant platter of blanched vegetables, tofu and lontong bound together by a rich peanut sauce.

foods.name: Soto
foods.description: A golden spiced broth with chicken, rice noodles and herbs — each region keeps its own beloved version.

foods.name: Pempek
foods.description: Savory fish cakes from Sumatra, served with a dark sweet-and-sour sauce of palm sugar and vinegar.

culture.title: Batik
culture.description: Wax-resist cloth dyed in intricate patterns, each motif carrying regional and symbolic meaning.

culture.title: Wayang
culture.description: Shadow puppetry of leather and light, where dalang storytellers animate epics through a screen.

culture.title: Gamelan
culture.description: Ensembles of bronze gongs, metallophones and drums producing shimmering, interlocking textures.

culture.title: Traditional Dance
culture.description: From the regal Legong of Bali to the war-like Tari Saman, dance carries the archipelago's stories.

culture.title: Traditional Houses
culture.description: Saddle-roofed tongkonan and floating rumah panggung — dwellings shaped by climate and kinship.

culture.title: Traditional Clothing
culture.description: Songket, ulos and tenun ikat — woven identities passed down through generations.

timeline.title: Ancient Kingdoms
timeline.description: Maritime empires such as Srivijaya and Majapahit dominate the straits, while Borobudur rises from the Kedu Plain.

timeline.title: Colonial Era
timeline.description: The Dutch East India Company and later the colonial state reshape the archipelago's trade and boundaries.

timeline.title: Independence
timeline.description: On 17 August 1945, Sukarno and Hatta proclaim Indonesian independence, igniting a revolution.

timeline.title: Modern Republic
timeline.description: Reformasi opens a new democratic era; a vast archipelago of seventeen thousand islands finds one voice.
